ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: As shown in the figure, the direction of a uniform magnetic field with magnetic induction intensity of magnitude B is obliquely upward to the right, and the acute angle it makes with the horizontal direction is $45^{\circ}$. A $\frac{3}{4}$ metal circular ring ab is placed in the magnetic field; the center of the circular ring is O, the radius is r, the two radii Oa and Ob are perpendicular to each other, and Oa is along the horizontal direction. When a current I is passed through the circular ring, what is the magnitude of the Ampere force on the circular ring?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The metal circular ring in the figure is a 3/4 circular ring missing the lower-left quarter, and the center of the circle is labeled O; point a is on the left side of O, the dashed line Oa is horizontally to the left, point b is below O, the dashed line Ob is vertically downward, and Oa and Ob are perpendicular. The current arrow on the arc shows that the current flows along the arc from a through the upper side and the right side to b. The arrow of magnetic field B is obliquely upward to the right, and the figure marks that it forms 45° with the horizontal direction. Reasoning: Take O as the coordinate origin, the x-axis horizontally to the right, and the y-axis vertically upward, then a=(-r,0), b=(0,-r). In a uniform magnetic field, the resultant Ampere force on a current-carrying wire of arbitrary shape is equivalent to F=I|\vec L\times \vec B|, where \vec L is the displacement vector from the starting point of the current to the ending point. The current goes from a to b, so \vec L=\vec r_b-\vec r_a=(0,-r)-(-r,0)=(r,-r), its magnitude |\vec L|=\sqrt{r^2+r^2}=\sqrt2 r, and its direction is 45° horizontally downward to the right. The direction of the magnetic field is 45° horizontally upward to the right, therefore \vec L and \vec B are perpendicular, and the included angle is 90°. Therefore the magnitude of the Ampere force is F=IB|\vec L|\sin90^\circ=IB\cdot\sqrt2 r=\sqrt2BIr.
